key_insight: Optimizing policies with vector-valued (multi-objective) rewards preserves response diversity in LLMs, producing a portfolio of behaviors that substantially improves the effectiveness of test-time search procedures like AlphaEvolve.
problem_solved: Standard post-training that optimizes a single scalar reward drives LLMs toward low-entropy, homogenous outputs, making them ill-suited to provide the diverse rollouts inference-time search needs to succeed in novel tasks and environments.
method: Replace a single scalar reward with a vector-valued reward signal that captures multiple task-relevant objectives or preferences.
Apply vector/multi-objective policy optimization (with diversity-encouraging regularization or latent conditioning) to train a model that yields a broad, high-entropy set of high-quality behaviors.

At inference, generate diverse rollouts from the trained model and feed them to a search/selection procedure (e.g., AlphaEvolve) which selects rollouts per task-specific reward, improving downstream performance.
impact: By training for diversity rather than a single optimum, practitioners get LLMs that are better building blocks for inference-time search—improving robustness and performance on novel tasks and enabling more effective inference-scaling methods.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: scalar-reward training (narrow cone of outputs) vs. vector-reward training (broad fan/portfolio of outputs).
Pipeline diagram: Vector Policy Optimization -> Diverse rollouts -> Inference-time search (AlphaEvolve) -> Selected best rollout.
Chart: diversity (entropy) and downstream search performance comparison between scalar-trained and vector-trained models.
Icon set: a multi-dimensional reward vector, a neural policy, and a magnifying glass selecting top rollouts (to represent search/selection).
paper_title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
paper_authors: Ryan Bahlous-Boldi, Isha Puri, Idan Shenfeld, Akarsh Kumar, Mehul Damani
